scope: Autonomous custom elements in the JS test runtime. Wistia validation was restricted to the six custom-element-related files requested by the user. No457-file or200-file sample and no performance comparison were run.
implemented: Document-bound lazy CustomElementRegistry and HTMLElement construction bridge; direct new and identity-preserving late upgrades with private fields.
define/get/getName/whenDefined/upgrade, constructor/name/duplicate validation and explicit rejection of unsupported definition types.
Synchronous programmatic creation, lazy parsed-tree and fragment upgrades, and HTML-namespace-only construction.
Observed attribute snapshots and connected/disconnected/adopted reactions with operation-boundary batching, nested reactions and backup microtasks.
Clone/import construction in parent-before-child order; target-registry import and original-definition adoption including closed shadow trees.
Registry/constructor isolation across windows, context disposal on reset/teardown and invalidation of discarded frame reactions.
Failed construction reports errors and cannot be retried; engine invariants use captured DOM methods rather than author overrides.
Allocation-free :defined matching; reaction queues allocate lazily only when a reaction exists.

focused_validation.includes: A custom element mounting a lazy React root, waiting for module readiness, signaling its effect, and unmounting on disconnection.

wistia_validation.interpretation: No new failing tests relative to the pre-change fork. The previously missing connectedCallback/import step now succeeds; the remaining React mount-marker failure matches jsdom. Two BaseLayout CSS failures also reproduce on the old fork.

mandatory_commit_hook.note: The existing mandatory native coverage/conformance hook runs automatically on source commits. The implementation validation selection remained custom-element tests only. An obsolete custom-element stub assertion upgrade() without a Node was strengthened to expect TypeError.

remaining_limits: Customized built-ins (is=/extends), form-associated custom elements/ElementInternals, scoped registries/initialize and moveBefore/connectedMoveCallback are not implemented. Unsupported definitions fail explicitly.
This runtime still shares DOM base prototypes and does not provide complete isolated JavaScript realms or browser navigation/script execution.
Namespaced attribute operations retain the existing DOM namespace API limitations; ordinary HTML observed-attribute callbacks are covered.
General DOM APIs and full web-platform custom-element conformance are not claimed; only the described autonomous subset and tests were validated.
The existing shared React application fixture failure and pre-existing CSS assertions remain open.
No new performance numbers are claimed. Ordinary query/selector paths acquire no custom-element per-node allocation; full performance comparison remains stopped.
